quest.title: Where the Koholasaurs Gather
quest.description: The predeparture preparations are complete. It's time to go to the location you and Mualani agreed on...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Where the Springs Return: Act III
chapter.title: Journey to the Mysterious Island

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're here, Mualani. Oh, and those strange scholars are here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Good morning, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: So when are we leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Haha, seems you're as excited as a child before the start of our journey.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: I just want to get down to business as soon as possible... You know this is no leisurely spring stroll, so I hope we can all act a little more professional.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm a very professional guide. Ahem, our journey to the mysterious island has officially begun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: First, do you all see this statue here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Is it an important clue?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, no. It's not a clue at all. He was the first chief of the People of the Springs who came back from the mysterious island and set up this place. It's a monument.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The first thing we need to do before we set off is to touch the statue and pray to our ancestors. This will make our journey to the mysterious island smoother.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Is there any theoretical basis to support that claim?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Theoretical basis? No, but my teacher taught me it's an essential step before heading to the mysterious island.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Very good! You didn't try to argue with me over something that you aren't knowledgeable about. That's very professional of you.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Sure, but since this practice doesn't have an empirical basis, I won't be able to include it in my thesis...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Come on, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Greetings to my ancestors. As your descendant, I'm about to follow in your footsteps and witness your accomplishments. Allow me to depart under your gaze and return under your protective watch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It really feels like we're about to embark on a great adventure!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Now, please get ready. We're going to look for the first clue.

talks.objective: Go to the location designated by Mualani

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, there are a lot of Koholasaurs here!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: As expected, the first clue is related to the Koholasaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: When people from outside the tribe get a copy of the map, most can deduce that the first clue is related to the Koholasaurs, but they often end up looking in the wrong direction.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: When the first chief created the map, he left a special mark for this part. It's a code that the tribe uses to indicate a herd of them.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So, it'll be impossible to gain any leads from just finding one or two stray Koholasaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're a real pro at this, Mualani!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: But according to the information I've been able to find, Koholasaurs don't like gathering as herds unless it's to compete for the hot springs...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So let me tell you a secret that only a guide from the People of the Springs would know. It so happens that wild Koholasaurs periodically gather in the valley up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's almost like how our tribe gathers together for festivals. Still, as soon as the season changes, the herd quickly disperses again.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Unless you're a guide who's always running across Natlan, it would be very rare to ever witness such a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: This is a thing!? I need to note this down right away, and include an explanation as a part of my thesis...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: According to what I've deciphered from the map, a clue is hidden deep in that valley.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But to get there, won't we have to get through the herd of Koholasaurs?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hmm, we'll have to think of a way to sneak past without startling them. They're gathering together with their friends, so I'm sure they don't want to be disturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: You mean, we're going to have to walk through the Koholasaur herd? That feels a little...

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Ahem... Given we've agreed to work together, everyone should do their part. However, Karya has been attacked by Koholasaurs before, so this isn't an ideal plan for her.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: But it shouldn't be a problem at all for me! Let's have Karya wait here and I'll take over all the tasks that were supposed to be entrusted to her.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, no worries. We don't need everyone to go.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #We actually need someone to stay and look after the luggage, so we'll leave that to you two. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Is that so? Then that works out perfectly.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: And now I understand how much you care for your assistant scholar.

talks.objective: Try going deeper into the valley

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These Koholasaurs sure seem on guard. We'll never get through...

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Given you've already used the information provided by the map to deduce that the clue is in that valley, why don't you simply chase them away? You're pretty strong, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: First of all, the elders of the tribe have always warned us to never hurt the Koholasaurs. Doing so will almost certainly bring bad luck.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: And secondly, you can't just show up and intrude on others' gatherings, much less make them leave! That's just terrible!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: But on what basis...

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Okay, so can we figure out another way to enter the valley?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hmm, there must be a way to enter the valley without startling them. It'd take a while for me to come up with a solution on my own, so I'd like to ask everyone to help come up with some ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon think... is there a detour or another way around?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: According to the map, the clue is right in the middle of the Koholasaur herd. Even if we try to approach from the other side, we'll just run into the same problem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, this is tricky...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Karya, I've noticed that you only talk when you're trying to help smooth things over between Viramdra and the others. I'm sure you must have some ideas of your own, so why don't you share them with us?

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Me? Alright... When Viramdra decided to look for leads on the Koholasaurs, I wanted to help, and so, I also looked up some information about the creatures.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: I discovered something very interesting... We thought that the Koholasaurs relied on their hearing to track their prey, but they also possess a very keen sense of smell.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: But, I'm not sure how useful that information is...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh... oh! That was actually very useful, Miss Karya!

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: You can just call me Karya.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #In that case, please stay here and keep an eye on the luggage. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me. I've got an idea!

talks.objective: Follow Mualani and find a way to infiltrate

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We must be getting close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, a bunch are gathering around that rock. What're they doing?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hmm, maybe when things start to get boring, they gather together and talk about something fun? Too bad I can't understand what they're saying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, Paimon thought guides from the People of the Springs could understand Koholasaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Sounds like someone has been trying to trick you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: True, they were definitely trying to scam us... Huh? Do you see that on the rock? It looks like some kind of... drawing?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I've heard that there is a type of moss that changes color when it reacts to the biological signals released by Koholasaurs. But to trigger that sort of reaction, you'd need a huge number of Koholasaurs...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That must be the clue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we take a picture?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The flash might disturb them. Let me try to copy it down.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Mualani copies down the mossy drawing and quietly leads you back the way you came. You then tell the patiently waiting Viramdra and Karya everything you saw and heard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we've passed the first stage of the journey now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: I see... Had we chosen to drive the Koholasaurs off, then we never would've found this lead... Seems there was a logical basis for everything you said after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Has he always been this way, Miss Karya?

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: He's just obsessed with his research, that's all...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: At least this has shown that my judgment is correct. I've proven my trustworthiness. And so, there should be no need for us to argue next time.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Yes, I understand... and I suppose that'll help us avoid wasting time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani really knows how to lead our group!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She is a professional guide, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Next, we'll need to use the lead we found to uncover our next destination. Now, what does this pattern represent?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hard to tell... Paimon certainly doesn't have any idea what it's trying to get at.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Aha! I got it!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Though the lines are kinda rough, I can still see that they represent the boundaries between the water and the land at Jadeskirt Knoll. We can use this to fill in the hole on the map and...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Find our next destination!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? You got all that just from some rough lines?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, intuition is also a part of it. Maybe I've just seen too many maps as a guide, and now it's easier for me to pick up on patterns like that.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, break time is over, let's get ready to move!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Found it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this...?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The key to making our way through the herd!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: If the Koholasaurs have a keen sense of smell, then even if we try to sneak around and stay out of sight, they'll still notice us once we get close enough.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But this plant can help us solve that problem, because its fragrance is very similar to the scent of a Koholasaur.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We can apply the plant's extract to our bodies and trick their sense of smell!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we're gonna... rub plant juice on ourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's also good for your skin.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Mualani collects some of the plant's extract and masks everyone with its fragrance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon feels all wet and slimy... but this actually does smell like a Koholasaur!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Perfect! Okay, let's try to make our way through again!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Mualani leads you into a valley where a herd of roaming Koholasaurs gathers. You must approach with caution...

talks.objective: Examine the graffiti on the stone wall

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Why can't we just chase the Koholasaurs away?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: How much I care? I was just trying to practice good crew resource management.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Viramdra and I will keep an eye on the luggage. We'll leave the rest to you!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You're too far from Mualani...

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Good luck! I'll keep an eye on the luggage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's about time to meet up now. Let's head to the spot Mualani mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, where should we look for the clue?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Heh, at a place where many gather... like a party!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Follow me and stay close.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: This way! If you go now, they'll definitely take note of us.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Be sure to stay out of sight!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What's that sound!? Careful!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: How could there be so many here? We can't get through...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, I have an idea. Wait here!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Noot-noot!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Come on!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Careful, don't startle them.
